trigger: a half-open TCP connection or CDN stall mid-transfer
summary: curl calls have only --connect-timeout, so a stalled 72 MB transfer holds one of the two macOS agents until the 90 minute job timeout. Also raised independently by build-ci, Fable and (UP-1) unhappy-path. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (--max-time, --speed-limit/--speed-time, --retry 8, step timeout-minutes 15)
classification_rationale: a missing bound in the step as written, not prose

trigger: the volume holding _temp fills during extraction
summary: UP-5: ENOSPC mid-extract left the 72 MB tarball and a partial tree on the full disk until the next job, so the other agent could hit ENOSPC too. Reproduced on a RAM volume. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (EXIT trap removes the root unless ok=1); re-verified on a nearly full volume

trigger: a redirect to a non-TLS URL
summary: curl -L could follow a redirect to plain http; the pinned hash makes it harmless but --proto-redir =https is free hardening. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (--proto =https --proto-redir =https)
classification_rationale: defence in depth in the step

trigger: an auditor reads the comment for the supply-chain evidence statement
summary: The rebar3 pin has no upstream provenance (no attestation or checksum asset) and the comment did not say so; recorded as trust-on-first-use of the bytes served 2026-10-14 (asset unchanged since 2024-08-29). FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (ci.yml comment and darwin-compat row state it)
classification_rationale: statement of an evidence limit, not a contradiction

trigger: a reader relies on the statistic
summary: The Erlang-step failure count was stated as "36 of 79" in the commit message, ci.yml comment, changelog and two docs. A census of the latest attempt per run gives 49 of 79 (a daily tally of first-attempt logs gives 48 of 78). The figure was the author's arithmetic slip. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (removed from ci.yml, docs and changelog; corrected in that commit message; PR body states 49 of 79)

trigger: a maintainer follows the hint after a Configure failure
summary: The "(CI: erlef/setup-beam)" hint edits in meson.build and assert-gateway-tests.py were not forced by the macOS change and were false for legs still on setup-beam. First reverted (0abc5e8d9). Kimi, Codex (adversarial review) and docs-writer (Gate 8) then showed the reverted text misleads on macOS and the Windows leg has no step of that name, so the wording is now leg-neutral ("this leg's Erlang install step in ci.yml"). FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (revert), 3f6fd4c76 and ef31d77e8 (leg-neutral wording)
classification_rationale: a hint naming an installer the leg does not use

trigger: a maintainer follows the bump advice
summary: Comments and ci-architecture.md said macOS uses "the same pin as the Linux leg" and told maintainers to move the Linux leg and release.yml together; the other legs float on 28 / 3.24 and macOS is exact-pinned. Raised independently by build-ci, cross-platform and Fable (and by docs, consistency, compliance and enterprise-readiness after being shown it). FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (wording, bump instructions: edit all four env values; Dependabot does not bump env values)
classification_rationale: prose contradicts the pins in the workflow

trigger: a later edit drops a sha check
summary: Nothing pinned the new macOS step: deleting either sha check or moving the install to the tool cache passed every test. A pin test was proposed and added (mutation-checked). FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (pin test added)
classification_rationale: a missing regression test (not a required-doc absence); rebar3 has no upstream attestation so its hash is its only integrity control

trigger: a maintainer opens the macOS docs to bump OTP or diagnose a hash mismatch
summary: The OTP/rebar3 bump procedure and what to do on a hash mismatch lived only in a ci.yml comment; Dependabot does not bump env pins. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (darwin-compat row, ci-architecture pointer, README pointer)
classification_rationale: routed-concern row for macOS pitfalls names docs/darwin-compat.md as the home for this procedure (item 6 of the required-doc list)

trigger: fork-controlled code runs earlier in the job
summary: UP-8: an earlier step of the same job can shadow shasum/openssl via GITHUB_PATH or BASH_ENV and make the check pass. Same user, same job, so no escalation; the hash check is integrity-against-CDN only. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (comment says the check does not defend against a compromised step in the same job)
classification_rationale: a limit on what the control defends against, stated in the comment

trigger: a customer reads the assembled changelog
summary: The fragment carried runner names, failure statistics and error strings for an internal CI change. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9 (shortened)

trigger: n/a
summary: Stray space before the closing parenthesis in the Erlang/OTP row. FIXED IN: 0abc5e8d9

trigger: a GitHub release CDN outage or rate limit
summary: Each macOS job now downloads 72 MB from github.com (setup-beam also did; the dependency is not new in kind). Mitigated by --retry 8 and the speed floor.

trigger: n/a
summary: The old /opt/ci/tool_cache/otp and /rebar3 trees (about 172 MB each) on the Minis are never pruned. Operator action: rm -rf them once on each Mini; recorded in the PR description because the owner cannot reach the boxes from this change.
classification_rationale: not a required doc; operational follow-up

trigger: a reader follows the pointer
summary: The Linux step comment says RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE is re-pointed "as on the macOS leg (see its step for the full reasoning, #4852)"; the macOS step no longer does that. Owner constraint: Linux leg untouched. Smallest fix is comment-only (drop the macOS pointer); stated in the PR description.
classification_rationale: a comment pointing at removed text

trigger: a trusted-fork run on the Linux leg
summary: The Linux leg's step-level RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE (trusted-fork isolation, #4852) is overwritten by the runner, so the declared isolation is not what setup-beam sees; the test asserts YAML intent only. Mechanism verified against actions/runner source (Kimi, Fable). Fable argues the consequence is nil today because setup-beam's tc.find never hits so no job executes a cached erl; Codex notes a working redirect would not stop later same-user fork code writing the cache, so a real boundary needs an OS identity. Kimi and Codex rated it MEDIUM (pre-existing, outside the macOS-only scope); derived here as I9 on the strength of the tc.find analysis, which neither reviewer refuted. Follow-up recorded in the PR description; not filed as an issue by this change.
classification_rationale: a control whose declared mechanism does not take effect

trigger: two macOS gateway ct runs overlap
summary: UP-6: both agents share one epmd on :4369 (#4853); an orphan epmd from a deleted install tree is reused. Unchanged by this diff, but jobs that previously died at the Erlang step now reach the multinode tests, so exposure rises. Watch the first paired runs.

trigger: both agents run rebar3 compile in the same second
summary: UP-7: both agents write ~yuzuci/.cache/rebar3 concurrently. Could not confirm rebar3 writes it non-atomically. Pre-existing and unchanged. Investigation owed: watch the first ten paired runs after merge for "Failed to fetch", "Failed to update registry", checksum or corrupt errors under .cache/rebar3.
waiver_rationale: speculative and pre-existing: not reachable from this diff; resolution by observation after merge

trigger: n/a

refuted_by: git show origin/dev:.github/workflows/release.yml | grep -n "setup-beam\|runs-on": setup-beam at 156 and 479 under runs-on yuzu-bigtam-linux; build-macos at 1000 has none
refuted_by_reporter: consistency-auditor (Gate 4, git grep origin/dev) and fable-review independently reached the same result; neither is the change's author

summary: CX-1/K2/K5: the first pin test accepted a commented-out verify and a third fetch with no verify. Found independently by Codex (comment-out) and Kimi (extra fetch). Both mutations reproduced. FIXED IN: 3f6fd4c76 (comment-stripped lexical gate plus nine in-memory mutations)
classification_rationale: test adequacy against docs/testing/unit-test-conventions.md (model gates on test_agent_ota_wiring_lexical.py)

trigger: a future edit weakens verify() or fetch()
summary: Gate 8: 27 reviewer mutations showed the gate still accepted: verify under if false, exit 0 before verify, verify()/fetch() stubbed, a second curl outside fetch(), a mismatch branch that no longer exits, hashing a fixed file, swapped pin/file pairs, set +e, continue-on-error. Found independently by quality-engineer, security-guardian and build-ci in the same wave. While fixing, my own mutation test caught a gap in the first draft of the verify() check. FIXED IN: ef31d77e8 (lexical gate extended; 19 + 4 mutations in test_macos_erlang_step_gate_rejects_regressions)

trigger: a future edit drops an env var from the step
summary: On bash 3.2.57 an "unbound variable" abort exits 0 once an EXIT trap is installed, so a step missing an env var would show green with no Erlang installed (reproduced on the target box). Unreachable today (pins are literals; RUNNER_TEMP and GITHUB_PATH are always set) - E6 caps it. Closed by validating every input before the trap is installed. FIXED IN: ef31d77e8 (check_pin and a reference to every variable before the trap; verified on the box: unset/empty/short pin and unset version all exit 1)
classification_rationale: latent wrong-result-as-success introduced by the round-1 trap

trigger: openssl fails or the file vanishes
summary: When openssl itself fails the step aborts with only openssl's stderr and no ::error:: annotation. FIXED IN: ef31d77e8 (could not hash <file>)

trigger: a Windows Configure failure
summary: The leg-neutral hint named the step "Install Erlang/OTP and rebar3", which the Windows leg does not have. FIXED IN: ef31d77e8 ("this leg's Erlang install step in ci.yml")

trigger: a very slow link or a typo in a version bump
summary: UP-G3: on a link between the 50 KB/s floor and about 120 KB/s the 72 MB download burns its --max-time per attempt and the 15 minute step timeout ends the step; a permanent 404 takes about 256 s. Both fail visibly and bounded; accepted.

trigger: SIGTERM delivered to the step shell only
summary: UP-G2: a bash-only SIGTERM can orphan a curl child that keeps writing an unlinked file; the runner kills the whole process tree and a verify mismatch would make any clobber visible. Accepted.
